subsystems.name: Neural interface
subsystems.role: records and stimulates neural activity at the resolution needed to detect or block injected signals.

subsystems.name: Signal processing
subsystems.role: amplifies, digitizes, and extracts features from neural signals in real time.

subsystems.name: Neural baseline model
subsystems.role: learns the user's normal patterns of activity for comparison.

subsystems.name: Anomaly detection engine
subsystems.role: flags signals that deviate from the baseline, indicating possible injection or alteration.

subsystems.name: Response and security layer
subsystems.role: blocks, attenuates, or alerts on suspicious signals, and authenticates external commands.

subsystems.name: Power and packaging
subsystems.role: supplies power and protects implanted electronics.

buildSteps.title: Develop a high-resolution bidirectional neural interface
buildSteps.detail: Current arrays record from hundreds of neurons; a cognitive firewall would need thousands to millions of channels and precise stimulation, approaching synaptic resolution—far beyond today's technology.

buildSteps.title: Build a real-time processing pipeline
buildSteps.detail: Signals must be amplified, digitized, and analyzed within milliseconds to catch an injection before it affects cognition.

buildSteps.title: Create a personalized neural baseline
buildSteps.detail: The system must learn the user's typical activity patterns across different mental states, requiring extensive calibration and adaptive models.

buildSteps.title: Train anomaly detection algorithms
buildSteps.detail: Using simulated attacks and recorded data, train classifiers to distinguish normal fluctuations from externally imposed patterns.

buildSteps.title: Implement a response mechanism
buildSteps.detail: When an anomaly is detected, the firewall could suppress the signal, stimulate a counter-pattern, or alert the user—each with its own risks.

buildSteps.title: Secure external communication
buildSteps.detail: Any wireless updates or commands must be authenticated and encrypted to prevent attackers from disabling the firewall or injecting commands.

buildSteps.title: Test in animal models, then human trials
buildSteps.detail: Ethical and safety review would be required; early tests might monitor for anomalies without active blocking.

buildSteps.title: Miniaturize and package for long-term implantation
buildSteps.detail: Power, cooling, and biocompatibility must be solved for a device that operates inside the brain for years.

prerequisites.why: current implants read from hundreds of neurons; synaptic-level read/write is not possible.
motor intentions can be decoded in lab settings, but complex thoughts and memories cannot.
we lack a complete theory of how thoughts and memories are represented, making it hard to identify unauthorized alterations.
cryptography exists, but implantable devices have severe power and size constraints.
electrodes degrade and scar tissue forms, limiting signal quality over time.

pathway.milestone: BCIs restore communication and movement for paralyzed people in research trials
pathway.unlocks: proof that neural signals can be read and interpreted in real time.

pathway.milestone: bidirectional BCIs with sensory feedback and limited memory prosthetics
pathway.unlocks: writing to the brain becomes possible, raising the need for security.

pathway.milestone: high-resolution interfaces and advanced decoding of cognitive states
pathway.unlocks: potential to detect anomalies, but also greater vulnerability to attack.

pathway.milestone: integrated cognitive firewall as a standard BCI security layer
pathway.unlocks: safer neural interfaces for medical and consumer use.
